html:
The Mississaugas of the Credit are an Anishinaabe (Ojibwe) First Nation in southern Ontario, named after the Credit River west of Toronto. Today their reserve is at New Credit, next to the Six Nations of the Grand River.

The Mississauga moved south from the north shore of Lake Huron around 1700 into land the Haudenosaunee had cleared in earlier wars. They fished salmon in the rivers flowing into Lake Ontario and traded with the French and British. Between 1781 and 1820 the British bought most of their land through a series of treaties, including the Toronto Purchase, on terms the Mississaugas disputed.

In the 1820s the Methodist minister Peter Jones, himself Mississauga, led his people in founding a farming village on the Credit; they moved to New Credit in 1847. In 2010 Canada settled their claim over the Toronto Purchase. See also Anishinabewaki and Odawa.
